title: Every simultaneous (p,q)-core partition is contained in the maximal (p,q)-core kappa_pq
canonical_url: https://mathdb.com/p/393907/containment-of-simultaneous-core-partitions-in-the-maximal-p (NOT accessed this session: MathDB 429 hold; statement taken hash-bound from frozen r339 proposals.json)

source_record.source_verified: Literal question found at PDF p. 19 = journal p. 913 of the retained full OWR article (Representations of Finite Groups, Oberwolfach Rep. 3 (2006) no. 2), in J.B. Olsson's abstract 'On block identities and block inclusions' (pp. 912-913). Verbatim: 'There is a unique partition kappa_pq of the maximum number (p^2-1)(q^2-1)/24, which is a p-core and a q-core. It is still an open question whether the Young diagram of any other partition which is a p-core and a q-core is contained in that of kappa_pq.' MathDB transcription matches literally (coprime positive p,q; rowwise containment lambda_i <= (kappa_pq)_i).
source_record.quantifier_notes: Scope: all coprime positive p,q. Edge cases p=1 or q=1: the only 1-core is the empty partition (every nonempty partition has a hook-1 corner cell), so kappa is the empty partition, unique, of size 0 = (1^2-1)(q^2-1)/24, and containment is trivial; the substantive case min(p,q) >= 2 is covered by the public proofs (Fayers assumes wlog s >= 2). 'Any other partition' vs 'every partition': equivalent (kappa contains itself trivially).

resolution.summary: The exact MathDB claim is a proven public theorem. First proved in full coprime generality by J. Vandehey (arXiv:0809.2134, 2008, Theorem 2.4 'Maximal Theorem' + Sections 4-5); independently proven and published peer-reviewed by M. Fayers, 'The t-core of an s-core', JCTA 118 (2011) 1525-1539, Theorem 5.1 / Proposition 5.5: 'Suppose s and t are coprime positive integers, and lambda is an (s,t)-core. Then [lambda] subseteq [kappa_{s,t}].' Olsson-Stanton themselves proved the t=s+1 case (Aequationes Math. 74 (2007) 90-110, Proposition 4.5) and posed the general case as their Remark 4.11 (= the OWR question).
theorem_labels: Fayers, JCTA 118 (2011) 1525-1539, Theorem 5.1 (with complete proof via Proposition 5.5, Lemmas 5.2-5.4)
Vandehey, arXiv:0809.2134, Theorem 2.4 (Maximal Theorem), proved via delta-sets in Sections 4-5
Olsson-Stanton, Aequationes Math. 74 (2007) 90-110, Theorem 4.1 (uniqueness/max size) + Proposition 4.5 (t=s+1 case)
resolution.chronology: question 2005/2006 (OS preprint Remark 4.11; OWR 2006/15 p.913) -> t=s+1 case OS07 Prop 4.5 -> full proof Vandehey Sep 2008 (arXiv:0809.2134) -> independent peer-reviewed proof Fayers 2011 JCTA -> cited as established (Aggarwal arXiv:1408.0550 'answered in the affirmative first by Vandehey and later by Fayers independently'; Thiel-Williams arXiv:1508.05293 Thm 1.3 remark).

applicability_bridge.statement_translation: MathDB kappa_pq (unique (p,q)-core of maximal size (p^2-1)(q^2-1)/24, existence/uniqueness by Olsson-Stanton Theorem 4.1) is the same partition as Fayers'/Vandehey's kappa_{s,t} (the beta_{s,t}-maximal core, whose beta-set is the (s,t)-closure of {st-s-t}, and whose size is (s^2-1)(t^2-1)/24; size cross-checked for 15 control pairs in sources/crosscheck-maximal-beta-set.json against the frozen r339 enumeration).
applicability_bridge.containment_translation: MathDB rowwise containment lambda_i <= (kappa_pq)_i for all i is exactly Young-diagram inclusion [lambda] subseteq [kappa] for left-justified Ferrers diagrams, the literal conclusion of Fayers Theorem 5.1 and of Vandehey's partition-wise containment beta prec beta_{s,t} (Vandehey's order: P(beta)_i <= P(beta')_i, i.e. rowwise).
applicability_bridge.conventions: s-core = partition with no hook length divisible by s (beta-set downward-closed criterion) — same in MathDB, Vandehey, Fayers, and the frozen r339 verifier. Fayers' proof is via the affine symmetric group action on alcoves and s-points; Vandehey's via beta-set/delta-set closure; both are complete and convention-exact. Olsson-Stanton Remark 4.10 warns that beta-set SET-inclusion does NOT imply diagram containment; the published proofs do not rely on that false implication.
applicability_bridge.scope: All coprime positive p,q: min(p,q) >= 2 by Fayers Theorem 5.1 / Vandehey Theorem 2.4 (Fayers states s >= 2, wlog s = min); p=1 or q=1 trivial (only the empty partition is a 1-core); p=q=1 trivial.
